notes.contentHtml:
Thank you for your interest in Cal Poly Maritime Academy!

California Polytechnic State University, San Luis Obispo and Cal Poly Maritime Academy has integrated into one university with two locations. Cal Poly Maritime Academy will be known as Solano Campus. Each respective campus will maintain separate assist.org accounts until Fall 2028, when our curriculum is fully integrated.


This articulation agreement displays the lower-division courses required in major and support. Students are advised to complete as much lower-division course preparation as possible prior to transfer.

GENERAL INFORMATION

  • University Catalog for the full listing of degree requirements for this major
  • Admissions website for current transfer admission requirements for Solano campus
  • Cal Poly Maritime Academy website for information for Solano campus 

ACADEMIC INFORMATION

  • Requirements and flowcharts for each major can be viewed on the respective major page, under the requirements tab. Information about concentrations, if applicable, are displayed on this page
  • AP/IB/CLEP credit
  • Academic Advising
  • Transfer Credits at Cal Poly | Cal Poly and Cal Poly Maritime Academy are one university with two locations. There will be two separate Assist.org accounts until Fall 2028, when our curriculum is fully integrated.


This is not a static document; new articulation may be added at any time. The information provided herein is subject to change without notice and does not constitute a contract or the terms and conditions of a contract between the student and the institution or the California State University.

notes.content: The Bachelor of Science in Oceanography requires a minimum of 120 units consisting of general education, major, and graduation requirements. This agreement only lists the lower division major requirements that may be fulfilled at the community college. The oceanography degree emphasizes workforce-ready skills and the development of professional networks that are crucial for successful placement after graduation. The global nature of the maritime sector is central for Cal Poly Maritime’s identity. Oceanography students gain an appreciation of global perspectives of ocean literacy and stewardship. Our graduates are prepared to serve as leaders in the development of new ocean science knowledge and the ability to make responsible, evidence-based decisions for managing ocean resources. Oceanography curriculum

The Bachelor of Science in Oceanography requires a minimum of 120 units consisting of general education, major, and graduation requirements. This agreement only lists the lower division major requirements that may be fulfilled at the community college.


The oceanography degree emphasizes workforce-ready skills and the development of professional networks that are crucial for successful placement after graduation. The global nature of the maritime sector is central for Cal Poly Maritime’s identity.

Oceanography students gain an appreciation of global perspectives of ocean literacy and stewardship. Our graduates are prepared to serve as leaders in the development of new ocean science knowledge and the ability to make responsible, evidence-based decisions for managing ocean resources.
